title_en: Sarah Guo - Funding the Frontier - [Invest Like the Best, EP.489]
title_zh: Sarah Guo（Conviction）：为前沿提供资金 —— Invest Like the Best EP.489
subtitle_zh: Conviction 创始人 Sarah Guo 谈前沿实验室豪赌、算力与开源之争、信念式投资与执行之道。
summary_zh: 本期 Invest Like the Best（EP.489）中，Patrick O'Shaughnessy 对话 Conviction 创始人 Sarah Guo，核心议题是在少数几家前沿实验室（frontier labs）与其余所有人之间正在拉开的分野上，一位早期投资人如何下注。Guo 自陈相信历史的“伟大人物”理论：在关键节点上，能动性极强的人若获得正确的风险资本、网络与环境支撑，确实能改变结果；开源模型的命运、美国产业政策、会不会出现有竞争力的西方开源模型，取决于有没有人做出来、能否募到钱、愿不愿投入资本与人才、建好基础设施去为前沿而战。但她否认这是一场战争：她与实验室的人紧密合作、共同投资，也反对“拥有一两个前沿模型的人会吞掉整个经济”的极端预期；她的志向不是成为那位“伟大女性”，而是在所选领域做最好的投资人，转向投资人身份源于极强的好奇心。节目用相当篇幅讨论算力与开源之争：当决定性问题变成“我需要 7,500 亿美元的算力开支”，个体与结果的关联感会被稀释；她因此押注廉价基础设施之上的千行百业生态，认为后训练、搭 harness 等技能的普惠化会让现实多样性远超前沿研究者的想象。方法论上她强调找到真相、确认它被错误定价、然后在别人转向前拿得住，并刻意把自己从噪声里保护出来；实例是 Conviction 作为 Chai Discovery 的第一张支票，该公司正与数家 top 10 制药公司合作加速研发流程，让她在 AI for biology 能否创造并捕获巨大价值的辩论中坚定站队。收尾落在她 23 岁被 Reid Hoffman 招进 Greylock、其后自建基金的历程，以及对 Ravi Gupta、Dylan Field、John Lilly 等早期给予信任者的感激。

turns.en: To learn more, visit psum.vc. So, where to begin? We'll hopefully be a really fun conversation. I guess because you and I are interested in so many of the same things, I'm just curious what's on your mind today.
turns.zh: 了解更多请访问 psum.vc。那么，从哪里开始聊好呢？希望这会是一场特别有趣的对话。我猜因为我们俩感兴趣的东西有很多重叠，我就很好奇——你今天在想什么？

turns.en: I think we're both feeling a little frenzied, and it's been going for a while, and it kind of feels like if anything, it might get more frenzied and more chaotic, both for what you do, but also the world around what you do.
turns.zh: 我觉得我们俩都有点被那种狂热裹挟的感觉，而且已经持续一阵子了，甚至感觉只会更狂热、更混乱——既关系到你做的事业，也关系到你所处的大环境。

turns.en: So, just in this moment, what does it feel like? What's on your mind? An obvious thing for anyone thinking about how to navigate this period as an investor is just how does it unfold and how is it different from the past?
turns.zh: 所以就在当下，这是什么感觉？你在想什么？对任何一个思考如何穿越这个周期的投资人来说，一个显而易见的问题就是：这一切会如何展开？它和过去有什么不同？

turns.en: What do I do if I can't backtest? I was talking to a investor friend last night, and the analogy he gave me was, I keep saying I want to press the brakes as hard as I can, but I'm not doing it, going 90 miles an hour.
turns.zh: 如果我没法回测（backtest），我该怎么办？我昨晚还在跟一位投资人朋友聊，他打了个比方：'我一直说我要把刹车踩到底，可我根本没踩，车还以每小时 90 英里的速度在冲。'

turns.en: And I do think the question is, do you miss the opportunity on one side, or do you make the mistake of every boom bus cycle in technology history?
turns.zh: 我确实觉得问题在于：你要么错过另一边的机会，要么重蹈技术史上每一轮'繁荣—公交'式周期的覆辙。

turns.en: Especially if you combine that with, what does it mean when you're also four years into building a firm for the durability of the firm and the careers of the people, I think is a complex question.
turns.zh: 尤其当你还叠加了这一层：你创办基金才四年，要为基金的 durability、为合伙人的职业生涯做长期建设——我觉得这是个非常复杂的问题。

turns.en: Do you think that we got it right in the profile that we wrote, that you're sort of making a specific, I think we called it a wager, a bad positioning, whatever you want to call it, that there is a really important fundamental thing happening between a couple of labs in AI and everybody else, and that we need to sort of like take up arms to make sure we don't end up in like a very monolithic outcome?
turns.zh: 你觉得我们那篇人物特写写对了吗？我们好像称之为一个'赌注'、一种独特的定位——随你怎么叫——就是认为 AI 领域少数几家前沿实验室和所有人之间存在一个根本性的重大分野，我们必须拿起武器，确保最终不会走向一个非常垄断化的结局？

turns.en: Do you think about it that way? I would answer in a maybe different way, which is I believe in like the great man and great woman theories of history.
turns.zh: 你会这样看待它吗？我可能会用另一种方式回答：我相信历史有'伟大人物'理论——great man 和 great woman 理论。

turns.en: If you have very high agency people in all of these places and they have the correct risk capital or support in the network or environment, yeah, you change outcomes.
turns.zh: 如果这些关键节点上都有能动性极强的人，而且他们获得了正确的风险资本、网络和环境的支撑，是的，你就能改变结果。

turns.en: You look at very important questions of what happens to open source models and like U.S. industrial policy. If you think about the opportunity for the ecosystem in the future, is there going to be a competitive Western open source model?
turns.zh: 你会去看那些极其重要的问题：开源模型的命运如何？美国的产业政策怎么走？想想未来生态的机会——会不会出现一个有竞争力的西方开源模型？

turns.en: It actually leads to like, did anybody make one? Could they like raise the money or were they willing to commit the capital and gather the talent base, build all the infrastructure and fight for the frontier or not?
turns.zh: 这最终取决于：到底有没有人做出来？他们能不能募到钱？愿不愿意投入资本、聚合人才、建好基础设施，为前沿（frontier）而战？还是做不到？

turns.en: I definitely think that individual people and entrepreneurs can affect the outcome. I don't necessarily think of it as a war I am working closely with and co-invested with and have many friends at the labs.
turns.zh: 我确实认为个体和创业者能改变结果。但我并不一定把这看成一场'战争'——我跟实验室的人合作紧密、共同投资，也有很多朋友在里面。

turns.en: I think it's fair to say the extreme point of view that some folks may have in outside of those big labs of the owner of one, two, three frontier models consumes the economy.
turns.zh: 可以说，有些在那些大实验室之外的人持有极端观点：拥有这一两个、三个前沿模型的 owner 会'吞掉'整个经济。

turns.en: I do not want that future very clearly and I don't think we are going to end up there. Do you actively want to be a great woman in this sense of the theory?
turns.zh: 我很明确不想要那样的未来，也不觉得我们会走到那一步。那你主观上想成为那种意义上的'伟大女性'吗？

turns.en: No. I don't mean that from like a personal humility perspective, it's just like it's not my set of goals. I want to be the best investor in the things that I try to do.
turns.zh: 不想。我这么说不是出于个人层面的谦虚，只是那不是我的目标设定。我想做的是在我选择的领域里成为最好的投资人。

turns.en: So it's not out of lack of ambition or even confidence. I think some people are driven by like, I want to be the person that made this happen.
turns.zh: 所以这不是缺乏野心或信心。有些人是被'我要成为成就这件事的那个人'驱动的。

turns.en: I thought I was going to be like a software entrepreneur for the longest time. My decision that from an identity perspective, I was going to be an investor actually had a lot to do with the idea of I'm deeply curious.
turns.zh: 很长时间里我以为自己会去做软件创业者。从身份认同上决定去做投资人，其实很大程度上源于我这个人好奇心很重。

turns.en: I like to understand things. I like to be right. I'm very motivated by working with extraordinary people. If I have a set of skills using those to make them more successful, it's like a pretty good fit for early stage investing.
turns.zh: 我喜欢理解事物，喜欢做对，也极其渴望和非凡的人一起工作。如果我掌握的技能能用在他们身上、让他们更成功，那简直太适合做早期投资了。

turns.en: If I want to work with the very best people and I want the companies to have impact, the firm can support a movement and support change we want to see, but I don't think it has to be me.
turns.zh: 我想跟最好的人共事，想让公司产生影响力。基金可以支撑一场运动、推动我们想看到的改变，但我不觉得必须由'我'来当主角。

turns.en: If that's the goal, what does it take, do you think right now, to be the best in a very competitive environment? Undeniably, you've done really well so far.
turns.zh: 如果目标是这个，你觉得在如今这么竞争激烈的环境里，做到最好需要什么？不可否认，到目前为止你做得非常出色。

turns.en: I'm curious what it has taken to be that good and what you think it's going to take in the next year plus within horizon to be that good. I think it's been pretty simple so far.
turns.zh: 我很好奇你是怎么做到这么好的，以及在接下来一年多的视野里，你认为要保持这么好需要什么。我觉得到目前为止其实挺简单的。

turns.en: My read of the environment was the growth of firms and generational transitions that were happening meant that it wasn't the most competitive landscape in early that it has been and you had this massive technology transition happening and if you took the bet on understanding the technology and the community and approach it from first principles, you might have better access and make better decisions than others who are less focused.
turns.zh: 我对环境的判断是：基金的成长和代际交替，意味着那时的竞争格局并不是早期史上最激烈的，而一场巨大的技术转型正在发生。如果你押注于理解这项技术和这个社区，用第一性原理去思考，你可能就拥有比别人更好的触达、做出更好的决策——尤其是比起那些没那么专注的人。

turns.en: All you have to do is take the risk and be focused and then it's an execution play. That's one of those things that I think is pretty simple and is just hard, this effort.
turns.zh: 你只要敢于承担风险、保持专注，剩下的就是执行力问题。这种事属于'道理很简单、但做起来很难'的那一类。

turns.en: I think today it's actually been not that complicated. It's more about what your bar is for the people you work with and my partner Mike and I started with a set of pre-existing relationships and understanding and so I think that has been useful.
turns.zh: 我觉得今天其实也没那么复杂，更多在于你对共事之人的标准。我和合伙人 Mike 是靠一批既有的关系和相互了解起步的，我觉得这很有用。

turns.en: Surely, there must be more than just outworking everyone. Mike said something interesting to me a couple of weeks ago which was there's sort of 250-ish people that he thinks about or you guys think about that are some combination of entrepreneurs and researchers and doing the most interesting things on the frontier.
turns.zh: 但肯定不只是'比别人更拼'这么简单。几周前 Mike 跟我说了一件很有意思的事：他说有大概 250 个左右的人——他或者你们在关注的——是某种创业者与研究者的结合体，在前沿做最有意思的事情。

turns.en: Yes. The people that are actually showing up in the morning and pushing this whole thing forward and that one of your goals as a firm is to be as close to those people.
turns.zh: 是的，就是那些每天早上真正到场、推动整个事业向前的人，而你们基金的一个目标，就是离这些人越近越好。

turns.en: Know them all and be as close to them and support them in as many ways as possible. I really like that idea. It's a cool idea and that's more than just doing a bunch of meetings with people that are starting companies from the outside looking in from the cheap seats.
turns.zh: 认识他们所有人，尽可能贴近他们、在尽可能多的方面支持他们。我真的很喜欢这个理念，这是个很酷的想法，远比坐在外围观台上跟一堆刚创业的人见几面要强。

turns.en: It looks like there's more unique stuff going on than just the competition set was low and we focused more and we're executing better. I'm interested in the ingredients that have been so far a part of success.
turns.zh: 看起来，除了'竞争者少一些、我们更专注、执行更好'之外，还有更多独特的东西在起作用。我对那些成功的'配料'很感兴趣。

turns.en: I won't name them but there's one well-known LP that does the survey every year of what all the other fancy LPs who they most want to invest with.
turns.zh: 我不点名，但有一家很有名的 LP 每年做调查：问其他一线 LP 最想和谁投资。

turns.en: You're either number one or two. There's something going on both with the companies you've invested in, with the performance so far, with the market perception.
turns.zh: 你要么排第一、要么排第二。所以在你的公司、目前的表现、市场认知背后，一定有别的东西在起作用。

turns.en: There's something more than just, okay, it was a moment in time we worked really hard. I'm trying to get at those ingredients. That's why I'm pushing on it.
turns.zh: 肯定不只是'抓住时点、非常努力'这么简单。我就是想挖出那些配料，所以才一直追问。

turns.en: To the point of perhaps making a bet that others wouldn't. We thought very carefully about what markets are going to matter and what might be different about the founders that we look at in this era if we are right about capability growth and the breadth of impact that would just be not obvious to other people.
turns.zh: 说到做别人不会做的赌注：我们非常仔细地想过，如果我们关于能力增长和影响广度的判断是对的，那么哪些市场会重要、这个时代我们要找的创业者会有什么不同——而这些是别人看不明白的。

turns.en: Where's the biggest difference from the status quo? How does the framework change? I'll give you two examples. One of the things that we were really looking for in the first year was application areas, workflows and professions, tasks that we thought were a good fit for purpose for the models, which is a very technology forward approach.
turns.zh: 与现状最大的差别在哪？框架该怎么变？我举两个例子。第一年我们特别在找的是应用领域：工作流程、职业、任务——我们判断哪些跟模型天然适配。这是一个技术先行（technology forward）的思路。

turns.en: Lots of people will be like, this is nonsense. You got to think about the customer problem and working from the customer back is the only way.
turns.zh: 很多人会说：这纯属瞎扯，你得从客户问题出发，从客户往回推才是唯一正路。

turns.en: We want to do both. If you look at Harvey and the function of the law, rationally, if you think that we can do next token prediction with language and you knew that in late 2022, then law is structured language.
turns.zh: 我们两边都想做。你看 Harvey 和'法律'这个职能：如果你相信语言能做下一个 token 预测（next token prediction），而且你在 2022 年底就想明白了，那么理性地看——法律就是结构化的语言。

turns.en: I'm not a lawyer, but from the outside, I'm like, you need to read a lot of documents and we had retrieval and you need to generate text. There's a lot of precedent text, both inside firms and in common law and history.
turns.zh: 我不是律师，但从外行角度看：你们要读海量文件——正好我们有检索（retrieval）；你们要生成文本——而律所内部、普通法和历史里有大量先例文本。

turns.en: That feels like a really good match. We also took a very specific view of what is now possible and then what is valuable within what is possible and then who's aligned with us.
turns.zh: 这看起来就是天作之合。我们还对'当下什么是可能的、可能之中什么是有价值的、以及谁和我们同频'持有一个非常具体的观点。

turns.en: Winston and Gabe, they believed that AI would transform the practice of the law in a very AI-pilled way. We will do enormously complex work with lawyers.
turns.zh: Winston 和 Gabe 坚信 AI 会以非常'AI 化'（AI-pilled）的方式彻底改造法律执业：'我们会和律师一起完成极其复杂的工作。'

turns.en: I don't know when. It could be next year or five years from now, but from the kernel of I can look at a landlord-tenant agreement in California and answer a question, somewhat trivial, to I can project to doing a Activision Blizzard M&A and doing 85% of the work, that's leap.
turns.zh: 不知道是什么时候，可能是明年，也可能是五年后——但从'我能看一份加州的租房合同并回答一个多少有点琐碎的问题'这个起点，外推到'能做 Activision Blizzard 级别的并购、完成其中 85% 的工作'，这是巨大的跃迁。

turns.en: The thing that appealed to me in that moment was the ambition of what was possible then and the technical logic of why it would work. I think that's probably a different decision-making framework from how other people are approaching in that moment.
turns.zh: 那一刻真正打动我的，是'当时什么是可能的'那种雄心，以及'为什么能成'的技术逻辑。我觉得这套决策框架，可能跟别人在那一刻的思路不一样。

turns.en: What is that group talking about today, the 250 researcher frontiers group? What's the most interesting thing and the most notable difference between today and six months ago or 12 months ago or something?
turns.zh: 那批人——那 250 个最前沿的研究者——今天都在聊什么？和六个月前、十二个月前相比，最有意思的变化、最明显的不同是什么？

turns.en: It is a violently competitive landscape. I think that was true 12 months ago, but even more true than it was 24 and then 36. I think people are very concerned that it is a globally competitive landscape and there's insecurity in that because I think it's a bit narrative breaking as well.
turns.zh: 那是一片异常惨烈的竞争战场。我觉得十二个月前就如此，但比二十四、三十六个月前更甚。大家很在意这是全球性的竞争，这里面有不安，因为我觉得这也是一种叙事上的'破壁'。

turns.en: I'm going to describe a belief and then question the belief. The belief is with recursive self-improvement of AI research, models that can improve the models themselves, we are a year or two years away from some sort of exponential intelligence.
turns.zh: 我先陈述一个信念，然后再质疑它。这个信念是：随着 AI 研究的递归自我改进（recursive self-improvement）——能改进模型自身的模型——我们距离某种指数级智能只有一两年。

turns.en: I think that belief is new within the last 12 months for a lot of researchers. I'm a dream driver of it that we're two years away. Andre Karpathy will actually in a very self-aware way say, I've thought it was two years away for about 10 years.
turns.zh: 对很多研究者来说，这个信念是过去十二个月才形成的。我自己就是'两年内到达'这个梦想的践行者。Andrej Karpathy 会特别有自知之明地说：'我以为还有两年，这个念头持续了大概十年。'

turns.en: And he thinks that again, to be fair, who can say? I do think that there is some sense of the major labs are so compute-intensive and so large from a headcount perspective now that the sense of contribution of I can move the needle of open AI as 200 people.
turns.zh: 公平地说，他现在也这么想——谁能说得准呢？但我确实觉得，如今头部实验室算力如此密集、人员规模如此之大，'我作为 OpenAI 的 200 人之一也能拨动指针'这种贡献感——

turns.en: Not that many researchers. The question of how do we get there is really up to every single person. Now if the question is, well, I need $750 billion of compute spend and we have many thousands of people working on this problem, I think people feel less ownership of the outcome.
turns.zh: ——已经不那么强烈了。'我们怎么抵达那个未来'这个问题，其实取决于每一个人。但如果问题是'我需要 7,500 亿美元的算力开支，已有成千上万人在攻这个问题'，我觉得人们会觉得自己和结果的关系没那么重要了。

turns.en: Oh, that's interesting. So it's just like a function of getting compute. That's the thing that's going to push this thing over the line, not our own human efforts.
turns.zh: 哦，这很有意思。所以它变成了一个纯粹'拿到算力'的函数——决定性的东西是算力，而不是我们自己的努力。

turns.en: I definitely think there's a large contingent of researchers who would feel that one of two things is now true. What I do doesn't matter anyway because the model is going to do it.
turns.zh: 我确实认为有一大批研究者现在会觉得以下两点之一成立：第一，'反正我做什么都不重要，模型会替我做'；

turns.en: Or two, the only thing that matters is compute scale. And both of those are somewhat disempowering. So then what are they doing? If I believe both of those and I'm a top five researcher or something.
turns.zh: 第二，'唯一重要的是算力规模'。这两条都挺让人无力的。那他们会怎么做？如果我信了这两条，又恰好是排名前五的研究者——

turns.en: That says something about your psychology because you want to do something that matters. I think there's also a set of scientists who want to work on the thing, whether or not it matters that they're working on it.
turns.zh: 这就关乎你的心理了：你想做有意义的事。当然也有一批科学家，不管自己做的事重不重要，他们就是想研究那个东西。

turns.en: An entrepreneur asked me yesterday, I would not work on the companies if I felt like we couldn't change the outcomes a little bit for them. He asked me yesterday, would any of the companies that you backed not been backed without you at that round?
turns.zh: 昨天一位创业者问我——如果他觉得对一家公司的结局产生不了哪怕一点改变，他是不会去做那家公司的。他昨天问我：你投的公司里，有没有哪家在那轮如果没有你就不可能被投？

turns.en: Would people have just said no? 5%, 10% max? They're resourceful, really talented people. They find other investors. There are lots of smart investors in the world who want to take that risk.
turns.zh: 别人难道会说不吗？最多 5%、10% 吧。他们足智多谋、才华横溢，总能找到别的投资人。世界上聪明的、愿意承担那种风险的投资人太多了。

turns.en: Maybe they wouldn't have gone the next $100 million of compute. I don't think every researcher doing frontier work at these top couple labs right now feels like they're essential to the machine.
turns.zh: 也许他们后面那 1 亿美元的算力投入就不会那么走了。我不觉得今天在头部那几家实验室做前沿研究的每个研究者，都觉得自己是这台机器不可或缺的一环。

turns.en: What do you think is the unhealthiest part of everything going on right now? What worries you about what people are trying to accomplish and what are the things that you're most worried will inhibit the future that you want to see?
turns.zh: 你觉得眼下发生的一切里，最不健康的部分是什么？人们试图实现的东西里，你最担心什么？最可能阻碍你想要的未来的，是什么？

turns.en: I think compute is one, people I think understand that very well. The version of us having enough compute over the next five to 10 years, and people are very much thinking about like 2032 at this point at scale, I was talking to the leader for infrastructure at one of the hyperscalers earlier in the week, and he's like, there was nothing that was going to move the needle for us at sufficient scale before 2030.
turns.zh: 我觉得算力是一方面，大家对此已经很清楚了。关于未来五到十年算力够不够——人们其实已经在按 2032 年这个尺度思考了——这周我和一家超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）的基础设施负责人聊，他说：2030 年之前，没有什么能在足够大的规模上撼动局面。

turns.en: That's depressing. Where can we get sufficient natural gas? Americans and entrepreneurs have been able to build new technologies and new capabilities very, very quickly in the past.
turns.zh: 真让人沮丧。足够的天然气我们从哪儿搞？美国人也好、创业者也好，过去在快速建造新技术、新能力上从来没掉过链子。

turns.en: I don't think it is a technology or capability or capitalism problem. I think it is a regulatory problem and an alignment problem. And I don't mean like AI alignment.
turns.zh: 我不觉得这是技术、能力或者资本主义的问题。我觉得这是监管问题，也是共识问题——我说的不是 AI 对齐（alignment）那个意思。

turns.en: I mean, if you want to build data centers in New York, you need to convince the people of New York they should want data centers there or America should want data centers there.
turns.zh: 我是说，如果你想在纽约建数据中心，你得说服纽约人让他们欢迎数据中心建在那里，或者让全美国觉得数据中心该建在美国。

turns.en: If you want to make the price of nuclear competitive as base load power, then you need to convince people it's safe, and you need to allow enough construction of SMRs in order for the price to come down because we understand how that cost curve will change in theory.
turns.zh: 如果你想让核电作为基荷电力在价格上有竞争力，你得让人们相信它是安全的，还得允许足够多的小型模块化反应堆（SMR）开建，成本才降得下来——因为理论上我们都清楚那条成本曲线会怎么走。

turns.en: I don't think we lack the technical and entrepreneurial capability to build abundant cheap energy for the data centers. That's one. The physical supply chain is just a tough reality.
turns.zh: 我认为我们并不缺乏为数据中心建造充裕廉价能源的技术与创业能力，这是其一。其二，物理供应链是一个硬现实。

turns.en: That makes me worried that the learning to build things and having the tacit knowledge and the labor and the raw materials, that can't go as fast as software or even decision making.
turns.zh: 这让我担忧：'学会建造'这件事背后的默会知识（tacit knowledge）、劳动力和原材料，不可能像软件、甚至像决策那样快。

turns.en: The only way through that is through. We just have to invest in it. On the investing side of what worries me, I was talking to one of our founders, several of our founders who are researchers, and explaining that the quality of their storytelling and their ability to make the companies that's legible to investors is obviously very important to their success.
turns.zh: 唯一的出路就是径直穿过去，只有持续投入。在投资这一侧，让我担心的是——我和我们几家由研究者转型的创业者聊过，对他们来说，把故事讲好、让公司被投资人看懂，显然对成败至关重要。

turns.en: It's going to be a capex-intensive play up front. The reality of the financial landscape for all of these people is, I'm not a research scientist.
turns.zh: 前期将是非常重的资本开支（capex）打法。这些人所处的融资现实是：我不是研究科学家。

turns.en: You're not a research scientist. All of the capital is not a research scientist. It's on entrepreneurs to go explain their story. One of the challenges is there are a lot of people attempting to invest, as they should, in technology bets.
turns.zh: 你也不是研究科学家，所有的资本也都不是研究科学家。解释自己故事的担子全在创业者身上。

turns.en: It varies how much fundamental understanding there is. There's a lot of proxying of judgment to pedigree or to other legible signals. Who's invested?
turns.zh: 挑战之一是，很多人——他们也理应如此——在尝试下注技术，但他们对基本面的理解深浅不一。大量判断被'代理'给了门第出身或其他看得见的信号：谁投了？

turns.en: References are always good. Who are the referral sources? The decision making is less fundamental. If I asked an extraordinarily good investor friend, we had a debate like you do, and I was like, I don't understand.
turns.zh: 推荐信当然有用，引荐人是谁也很关键。但决策并不那么基于基本面。我一位极优秀的投资人朋友——他和我们之间也像咱俩这样辩论——我说：'我看不懂。'

turns.en: What is this company going to be that would be big? Explain it to me. His explanation was essentially, do you know the quality of this person?
turns.zh: '这家公司到底是什么？它凭什么能做这么大？你给我讲讲。'他的解释本质上就一句：'你知道这个人的水平有多高吗？'

turns.en: Yes, I've known the quality of the person for eight years. The technical theory in the business don't make sense to me. People are making large-scale research bets without any intuition for them or without any opinion on them.
turns.zh: '知道，我认识这个人八年了，知道他有多优秀。'可其中的技术理论和商业逻辑他讲不通。人们在没有任何直觉、也没有任何观点的情况下，就下重注押研究。

turns.en: I'm like, it's not all going to work. I may not be any better at deciding, but we want to get to that intuition. I think not having a point of view on the business besides the pedigree of the person is dangerous.
turns.zh: 我的反应是：这不可能全都成。也许我在决策上也不见得更高明，但我们想要的是那种直觉。我觉得，除了'这个人出身好'之外对生意本身没有观点，是危险的。

turns.zh: Vanta 把合规自动化，让你的团队少花时间应付安全审查，多花时间拿下客户。Vanta 能将审计准备时间削减 82%，给你即时、最新的信任凭证，告别大量手工劳动，帮你更快、更少摩擦地成交。

turns.en: Customers report a 526% return on investment, and more than 16,000 companies use Vanta, including Ramp, Harvey, and Snowflake. Get started with $1,000 off at vanta.com slash invest.
turns.zh: 客户反馈投资回报率高达 526%，超过 16,000 家公司在用 Vanta，包括 Ramp、Harvey 和 Snowflake。到 vanta.com/invest 开始使用，立减 1,000 美元。

turns.en: Ridgeline is the first end-to-end system of record with embedded AI for investment management firms running portfolio accounting, reconciliation, reporting, trading, and compliance on one unified platform.
turns.zh: Ridgeline 是首个内嵌 AI 的端到端记录系统（system of record），面向投资管理公司，在一个统一平台上完成组合核算、对账、报表、交易和合规。

turns.en: Firms are moving off legacy technology and onto Ridgeline because of how far ahead Ridgeline's AI features are compared to anything else in investment management software.
turns.zh: 越来越多公司正从遗留系统迁移到 Ridgeline，因为它的 AI 功能比投资管理软件里的任何其他产品都领先一大截。

turns.en: I've been hearing from a lot of investment managers about AI, and they fall roughly into two camps, with some unsure where to even start and others convinced they can build their own order management system over a weekend.
turns.zh: 我听很多投资管理人聊 AI，他们大致分两派：一派完全不知从何下手，另一派坚信自己一个周末就能手搓一套订单管理系统。

turns.en: The reality is that running an investment firm will always require governance, controls, and a single source of truth for your data. And no amount of AI enthusiasm changes that requirement.
turns.zh: 现实是，经营一家投资公司永远需要治理、控制，以及你数据的唯一真相源（single source of truth）。再多的 AI 热情也改变不了这个要求。

turns.en: Ridgeline is built on exactly that foundation, which is why I believe that the firms that come out ahead in the AI era will be the ones running on Ridgeline's unified platform.
turns.zh: Ridgeline 正是建立在这个基础之上，所以我相信，AI 时代胜出的公司，会是那些跑在 Ridgeline 统一平台上的公司。

turns.en: If you're serious about your firm's AI strategy, Ridgeline should be part of that conversation, and you can request a demo at ridgeline.ai. Who is a researcher that has most blown you away, and how did they do so?
turns.zh: 如果你的公司认真考虑 AI 战略，Ridgeline 应该进入你们的对话，可以上 ridgeline.ai 申请演示。——哪位研究者最让你震惊？是怎么做到的？

turns.en: What's something that they did that to you felt extraordinary back to the great person theory? There are a number of these people who I think the history books will write about, a contribution of theirs as a truly extraordinary thing that created this kink.
turns.zh: 他们做过什么让你觉得非凡的事？回到'伟大人物'理论——有几位这样的人，我觉得历史书会写下他们的贡献，那是真正非凡的、造成了某个历史弯折的贡献。

turns.en: What's an example of a person like that and something that you've seen them do? My partner Pranav and I were introduced to Tony Zhao and Cheng Chi at Sunday Robotics when they were PhD students at Stanford.
turns.zh: 能举一个这样的人、一件你亲眼见过的事吗？——我和合伙人 Pranav 认识 Tony Zhao 和 Cheng Chi 的时候，他们还是斯坦福的博士生，后来创办了 Dyna Robotics。

turns.en: They worked at Toyota Research and DeepMind and Tesla, and so they weren't just academics by any means. There were young PhD students who I think were like 25.
turns.zh: 他们在 Toyota Research、DeepMind 和 Tesla 都工作过，绝不是纯学术背景。当时是很年轻的博士生，我记得大概 25 岁。

turns.en: I think one of them didn't finish, they just started the company. What I thought was impressive about them then and then now, I remember looking at their body of work took me a while to get oriented, but I think that they have contributed dual-handedly most of the interesting ideas in robotics AI over the last four years.
turns.zh: 其中一个好像都没读完博士，直接去创业了。他们从当时到现在都让我印象深刻——我记得他们的研究体系我得花一番功夫才能看懂——但我认为过去四年机器人 AI 领域最有意思的想法，几乎都出自他俩之手。

turns.en: That's a pretty weird thing for two very young people to do. If I try to characterize the type of ideas, it is, how can I use modern AI to solve the robotics generalization and robustness problem in a very practical way?
turns.zh: 这对两个非常年轻的人来说很不寻常。如果非要概括他们想法的类型，那就是：怎么用现代 AI，以非常务实的方式解决机器人的泛化与鲁棒性问题？

turns.en: It is believed in robotics that if we just had the internet of robotics data, yeah, we'd have fully general robots everywhere, this is clearly going to work.
turns.zh: 机器人领域有一个信念：只要我们有'机器人数据的互联网'，到处都会有完全通用的机器人——这事显然能成。

turns.en: One of the big research and practical problems is like, where do you get that data? Some of the ideas that Tony and Cheng have worked on is, how can you be clever about collecting the data in the cheapest way possible in a way that supports the distribution of real-world environments and tasks?
turns.zh: 研究和实践的一大难题是：数据从哪来？Tony 和 Cheng 做的一些工作就是：怎么用尽可能便宜的方式聪明地采集数据，同时支撑真实世界环境和任务的分布。

turns.en: I think the creativity of thinking about the actual constraints, we don't have the data, we don't have incident dollars to spend on the data, and we're going to treat it as a technical problem to solve of the shape of the data and the collection and how to interact with the model and how much of a cheap data collection can we transfer to model learning.
turns.zh: 我觉得那种针对真实约束的创造性思考特别精彩：我们没有数据，没有天文数字的钱去砸数据，那就把数据的形状、采集方式、如何与模型交互、多少廉价采集能转化为模型学习，当成一个技术问题去解决。

turns.en: That's super interesting, that's very outcomes-driven. I was blown away in the first meeting, we said yes immediately there, thankfully. It's just under two years that the company has been around.
turns.zh: 太有意思了，完全是结果导向。第一次开会我就被震住了，我们当场立刻说'投'，谢天谢地。这家公司成立还不到两年。

turns.en: Nothing is true until it is shipped. This entire team believes that we are going to have general, semi-humanoid robots doing things in people's homes, first and beta end of this year.
turns.zh: '东西没做出来之前都不算数'——但这整个团队相信：到今年年底，我们就会看到通用的半人形机器人在人们家里干活，先上 beta。

turns.en: That is not something that any of us believed. It blows me away that you can move that quickly from a bunch of cardboard in a Stanford basement to the full stack thing that is manufactured here.
turns.zh: 这是我们谁都不曾相信的事。让我惊叹的是，他们能从斯坦福地下室里的一堆硬纸板，这么快推进到如今全栈自研、在这里制造的产品。

turns.en: We have done hundreds of iterations of hardware on model data collection and translated it into tasks and tested it in all these real-world environments.
turns.zh: '我们针对模型的数据采集已经迭代了上百次硬件，把采集转化为任务，并在所有这些真实环境里做了测试。'

turns.en: It's going to work. Committees are very cool. The speed of that is mind-boggling. I still think the broad view, not everyone, but lots of people in Robots are like, now it's a question of when, not if.
turns.zh: '这一定会成，他们那种全情投入特别酷，速度快得令人咋舌。'我还是觉得，从整体看——不是所有人，但机器人领域很多人——现在的态度已经是'只是时间问题，不是能不能的问题'。

turns.en: It surprised me that the team was like, if not this year, next year. I'm very curious about the moments of your investment decisions. You just said in the first meeting you were sort of like, we're in.
turns.zh: 团队说'不是今年就是明年'，这一点让我很意外。我很好奇你做投资决策的那些时刻。你刚说第一次见面基本就是'我们上了'。

turns.en: Is it always like that, or are there examples of things where you like hem and haw? You end up doing it and it works. I would love to hear more about how you and your team make investment decisions.
turns.zh: 每次都这样吗？还是也有犹豫拉扯、最后还是投了、结果又成的例子？我很想多听听你和你的团队怎么做投资决策——

turns.en: The actual in-the-room process for, okay, this thing is interesting. We're going to do it or we're not. We're debating it. What is that process?
turns.zh: 真正在那个房间里，'这东西有意思，我们做还是不做、我们来辩论'的那个过程，到底是什么样的？

turns.en: What is it like? It varies based on company. I'm very instinctive on people. I often know I want to do something immediately. If I know what somebody has worked on and then I interact with them and I hear the idea and I have some basis, some background in the idea, we have a rating scale, a one to 10 scale.
turns.zh: 因公司而异。我对人是靠直觉的，常常马上就想知道我想不想做这件事。如果我了解一个人做过什么，又和他交流过、听到了他的想法，而我在这个想法上也有些背景和基础——我们有一个 1 到 10 的打分制。

turns.en: I'm like immediately an eight or a nine. What I'm then doing between that and a real decision is often figuring out what are the holes in my understanding, where my judgment of their premise or them is incomplete or wrong.
turns.zh: 我往往一上来就打 8 分或 9 分。从那一刻到真正做决策之间，我要做的常常是搞清楚：我的理解哪里有漏洞？我对他们前提、或者对他们这个人的判断，哪里不完整或错了？

turns.en: What do I not know? If you're in a master looking for the most ambitious, impactful companies, you can't know every domain. We have biology and defense and robotics and law.
turns.zh: 我还有哪些不知道？如果你做的是一支寻找最有雄心、最有影响力公司的基金，你不可能懂每一个领域——我们有生物、国防、机器人、法律。

turns.en: I'm spending the next day to a few weeks desperately trying to ground myself and being like, okay, what does everybody else believe about this space?
turns.zh: 接下来的一天到几周里，我会拼命给自己补地基：关于这个领域，别人都相信什么？

turns.en: Are they the people I think they are? That's what my process looks like. And then I want to get feedback. I want to get second reads on people.
turns.zh: 这些人真的是我认为的那种人吗？我的过程大体如此。然后我想要反馈，想要别人对这个人做二次判断。

turns.en: I want to understand what the core questions are. I'm a memo person. Even at the very beginning of the firm, when it was just me, I would write the full memo, perhaps Greylock style, ship it off to a friend that was an investor who I trusted for their perspective outside of the funds.
turns.zh: 我想搞清楚核心问题是什么。我是个写备忘录（memo）的人。哪怕在基金最早期、只有我一个人的时候，我也会写完整的备忘录，也许是 Greylock 风格，然后发给我信任的一位、基金体系之外的投资人朋友。

turns.en: You and I have talked about what do you value about a partnership? I'm like, I'm comfortable making investment decisions, but I think other people can make me better.
turns.zh: 你我聊过：你重视合伙关系的什么？我的感觉是，我自己做投资决策没问题，但别人能让我更好。

turns.en: I want people to push with the logic and have me reflect. So I used to take the memo and send it to John Lilley or Dillon Field or something.
turns.zh: 我希望别人拿逻辑来推我、让我复盘。以前我会把备忘录发给 John Lilly 或 Dylan Field 他们看。

turns.en: When we were in a memo, I'd go see what Bella or Pranav or Mike wants to know about the person, try to complete the picture. Other people I think are more even in their decision making.
turns.zh: 不写备忘录的时候，我就去问 Bella、Pranav 或 Mike：关于这个人你们想知道什么？努力把这幅拼图补全。有些人做决策的方式比我更'均衡'。

turns.en: They're thinking about it and thinking about it. They climb to conviction versus I start there and then I work backwards. But I think a similarity between both Mike and I is we'll start at a point and explain what will move us.
turns.zh: 他们反复掂量、一点点爬到信心高点；我是先站定在高处，再往回倒推。但我和 Mike 有个共同点：我们会先亮出一个起点，然后说明什么会动摇我们。

turns.en: I met a really interesting company earlier this week with my partner, Bella. And I'm like, okay, instinctively, I am positive on it, but I don't know enough about the science here.
turns.zh: 本周我和合伙人 Bella 见了一家很有意思的公司。我的直觉是：我看好它，但这里的科学我不够懂。

turns.en: And I have to go make sure this makes sense. Can you really be an eight or a nine if you don't get it? No, I couldn't get there. Now, as we were talking about, it is one of my concerns for this period of time.
turns.zh: 我得去确认这事站得住脚。'如果你不懂，你真的可能打出 8 分或 9 分吗？'——不能，我打不到。这其实也是我对当下这个阶段的担忧之一。

turns.en: I'm like, if you don't feel like you have any grounded intuition on the bet itself, what are we doing here? I'm trying to think about if that's fair.
turns.zh: 我在想：如果你对赌注本身没有落地的直觉，那我们在这儿干嘛？我也试着琢磨这种担忧是否公平。

turns.en: If Brett Taylor wanted to dig in volcanoes or do dog streaming or something, I'd be like, yeah, of course, man, but he wouldn't do that. There's some version of I don't even care if it doesn't compile in my brain.
turns.zh: 如果 Bret Taylor 想去做火山勘探、或者搞代遛狗之类的生意，我想我也会说：好啊当然，投就完了——但他不会做那种事。所以有某种版本是：哪怕在我脑子里说不通也无所谓，这个人好到不容置疑，我就直接投。

turns.en: The person is so undeniably good that I would just back them. Brett, that was an example. Yes. I feel like these things are so inextricably intertwined in my mind because part of what makes people great.
turns.zh: 'Bret 只是个例子。'对。在我心里这两样东西是分不开的，因为构成一个人伟大的部分——

turns.en: Like I was trying to help one of my companies, the candidate, yesterday. And they're like, oh, what did you see in these people? And I'm like, they're just so right.
turns.zh: 比如昨天我在帮我的一家公司看候选人。他们问：'你从这些人身上看到了什么？'我说：'他们就是总是对的。'

turns.en: He's right all the time. Their industrial logic is impeccable. They have all these great character traits too. They're amazing at recruiting, but they have a point of view that I think is going to be right in the world.
turns.zh: 他总是对的，他们的产业逻辑无懈可击。他们还有很多优秀的品格特质：特别会招人，而且他们有一套我认为是会应验的世界观。

turns.en: I've seen them just make repeatedly correct decisions, including when I am wrong. And I'm like, I have a lot of respect for that. When you say like these people are amazing and part of what I think makes them amazing is I believe in their judgment.
turns.zh: 我亲眼见过他们反复做出正确决策，包括我错的时候。我对这一点非常尊敬。当我说'这些人了不起'，了不起的一部分就是我相信他们的判断——

turns.en: I don't understand what they're doing. I can't have an opinion on their judgment. Brett's doing enterprise AI. I understand what he's doing.
turns.zh: 哪怕我并不理解他们在做什么，我没法对'他们的判断'本身发表意见。Bret 做企业级 AI（enterprise AI），这个我懂他在做什么。

turns.en: If I were to build a pie chart of your time now, not when you started the firm, but today, there's meeting new companies, there's helping existing companies, there's talking to researchers, there's time with other people, there's talking to candidates, I have no sense of what it would be.
turns.zh: 如果让我给你现在的时间画一张饼图——不是刚创办基金时，而是今天——有新公司会面、有帮已投公司、有和研究者交流、有和别的人相处、有看候选人——我完全说不上来占比。

turns.en: If you had to sum it up, what are the things that you spend your time on and what's the percentage allocation? I think I spend two thirds, three fifths of my time working on portfolio company stuff.
turns.zh: 如果非要概括：你的时间都花在哪、各占多少？我想我三分之二、五分之三的时间花在已投公司的事务上。

turns.en: And that is recruiting, helping people think through things, trying to influence the outside ecosystem in some way, then raising money. The next largest piece is looking at companies.
turns.zh: 包括招聘、帮人把事情想透、想办法影响外部生态，然后是募资。第二大块是看公司。

turns.en: I don't know if this is right or wrong, get paranoid about it and move the number, but I probably see four to six new companies a week. It's not a very high volume.
turns.zh: 不知道这算多还是少，我对这事挺 paranoid、总想把它往上推——但我大概每周只见四到六家新公司，量并不大。

turns.en: My first couple months, my old firm, I saw 500 companies and so I'm like, now I feel more calibration where I just have much more confidence I can tell.
turns.zh: 在上一家基金的最初几个月，我见了 500 家。所以现在我感觉校准度更高了，对自己'看得出来'这件事更有信心。

turns.en: The balance of my time, I am doing a combination of help one of my partners look at something, meet people that might teach me something about the world and that can be a researcher or if you are a purely early stage in a larger firm, even be very myopic because your ecosystem is big enough and we are a very small firm or ecosystem oriented and so I've learned so much from just getting to know investors who think differently than I do, including
turns.zh: 剩下的时间，我会帮合伙人看一些东西、见一些能教我认识世界的人——那可能是研究者；如果你是一家更大机构里纯做早期的，甚至可以很'井底'，因为你的生态足够大；而我们是一家很小的、生态导向的基金。我从结识那些和我思路不同的投资人身上学到了很多，包括——

turns.en: different asset classes. Well, I never spent that much time with public markets people before and it's just very educational how they think about the world.
turns.zh: ——不同资产类别的投资人。我以前从没花那么多时间和公开市场的人相处，他们对世界的思考方式真的很有教育意义。

turns.en: I spend time with other investors of all skills and asset classes. I spend time with companies right now with a pharma company who is thinking about how AI is going to transform their business.
turns.zh: 我和各种层级、各种资产类别的投资人交流。我现在也在跟一家制药公司打交道，他们在思考 AI 会如何改造自己的生意。

turns.en: This is very interesting to me because I've learned a lot about what they believe about the future. I've learned a lot but I'm like leaving room in my calendar for learning, feeding curiosity and then there are pieces that are other parts of bridges to DC, external communication.
turns.zh: 这对我很有意思，我从他们相信的未来里学到了很多东西。但我会在日程里给'学习和喂养好奇心'留出空间，剩下的还有通往 DC 的桥梁、对外沟通这些部分。

turns.en: What have you learned about raising money? I stand with the belief that I advise entrepreneurs with which is huge to understand people's objections to what you are doing and their questions but you should not tell them what they want to hear.
turns.zh: 募资上你学到了什么？我给创业者的一条信念同样适用于自己：理解别人对你所做之事的异议和问题非常重要，但你不应该去说他们想听的话。

turns.en: When I started the fundraise for fund one, I knew a lot of LPs over a long period of time already so it was not very complicated but I had one of my friends who is a private equity investor who stated, you have to have a very differentiated story for LPs.
turns.zh: 我募第一期基金时，很多 LP 早就认识了很长时间，所以不算复杂。但我一位做私募股权（private equity）的朋友说：'对 LP 你必须有高度差异化的故事。'

turns.en: Every part of the funnel should be the specific thing you're going to do and I'm like, let's be honest, I don't know yet but I need to raise the money so I can experiment and figure it out.
turns.zh: 漏斗的每一步都该是你具体要做的事。而我说：说实话，我还不知道，但我得先把钱募到手，才能去试验、去找答案。

turns.en: So I never made slides and told a specific story about all the things that we attempt to do now. I think you don't know until you make contact with reality and think about it and you're in the market, there were definitely LPs who did not like that.
turns.zh: 所以我从来没做过那种 PPT、把我们现在尝试的一切讲成一个具体的故事。我认为在接触现实、认真思考之前你不可能知道。在市场里，确实有 LP 不喜欢这样。

turns.en: I gave people a two-pager on my background and investing history and claimed that I was good at identifying extraordinary people, being useful to that set of people and being genuine supporters.
turns.zh: 我给大家的是一页两页纸：我的背景和投资历史，外加我声称自己擅长识别非凡的人、对这群人有实际用处、并且是真诚的助推者。

turns.en: You combine that with investment judgment and ability to recruit. You got a starting point. Some things I imagine about firm culture and then we'll go execute like hell and figure it out.
turns.zh: 再叠加投资判断力和招人能力，那就是一个起点。关于基金文化我想象了一些东西，然后我们就去拼命执行、边干边明白。

turns.en: I can see how this is tough from an LP perspective and I deeply value the people who bet on us early because they go write a memo for their investment committee and they're like, she's going to execute like hell, we'll find out.
turns.zh: 我能想象从 LP 视角这有多难。我深深感激那些早期就赌我们的人——他们给投委会写备忘录时大概会写：'她会玩命执行，走着瞧。'

turns.en: Sometimes the cleanliness of the story is what people are looking for. I can't advise other managers on this because people have different outcomes.
turns.zh: 有时候人们要的就是故事的干净利落。这个我没法给别人建议，因为大家的结果各不相同。

turns.en: If you tell people what you are going to do, life is much simpler and what you actually believe life is much simpler. For me as a master, when somebody can convince me that the world works differently than I thought, I'm immediately incredibly excited.
turns.zh: 如果你告诉别人你要做什么，生活会简单很多；讲你真正相信的东西，生活也会简单很多。对我而言，当有人能说服我'世界和我原以为的不一样'时，我立刻就兴奋得不行。

turns.en: Maybe I can convince people that this is just how it actually works. I've met a lot more investment managers for the last four years and I knew a lot of BCs, but people who are doing creative things, I really like entrepreneurial investment managers as you I think do and as you might imagine where I'm like, I don't want to build the firms that they've built, but the creativity with which Philippe and Thomas go to or that
turns.zh: 也许我能说服大家：世界本来就是这么运转的。过去四年我见了多得多的投资管理人。我以前认识不少 LP，但那些在做创造性事业的人——我真的很欣赏有创业精神的基金管理人，我想你也一样——

turns.en: Josh at Thrive approach their business and the encouragement they have for others to approach their business. Well, you can do new things and you should go express your opinions in the form of your investment management firm.
turns.zh: 就像你能想到的：我并不想建成他们那样的公司，但 Philippe 和 Thomas 经营自己公司时的那种创造力，还有 Josh 在 Thrive 的做法，以及他们鼓励别人用各自方式经营公司——'你可以做新东西，你应该用你的基金管理公司来表达你的观点'——

turns.en: I think it's amazing. What was imprinted on you watching your parents who are both entrepreneurs? I think this is very helpful to me because there was no moment of my childhood or being a teenager where I felt like they were not there for me, even though they worked all the time.
turns.zh: 我觉得这太棒了。你的父母都是创业者，他们给你留下了什么烙印？我觉得这对我帮助很大，因为我童年和青少年时期没有一个时刻觉得他们不在我身边——尽管他们一直在工作。

turns.en: Stop it. Both of them. If you try to resolve these things, that's pretty independent kid. That helps me. I don't know where I was in the distribution, but I feel like I was pretty independent.
turns.zh: 别说了别说了，他俩都是。你要是想平衡这些的话——我算是相当独立的小孩，这帮了我。我不知道自己在分布上处于哪个位置，但我感觉自己相当独立。

turns.en: It helps me to think your family can make you feel like you are the center of their world, their whole people with other interests and they want to spend time doing other things too.
turns.zh: 这让我这样看待事情：家人可以让你觉得你是他们的中心，同时他们也是有其他志趣的人，他们也想花时间做别的事。

turns.en: Even just recognize my own importance from the perspective of remembering what it's like to be 10 years old. I liked my mom. I love my mom and dad and it was so cool.
turns.zh: 哪怕只是通过回忆自己十岁时的感受，认清自己在别人世界里的分量。我喜欢我妈妈——我爱我爸爸妈妈，那真的很酷。

turns.en: Our family values are very similar to theirs. Integrity, thinking for yourself, independence of thought and then there's like focus on family, team spirit and family.
turns.zh: 我们家的价值观和他们很像：正直、独立思考、思想的独立性，然后还有重视家庭、团队精神和家人。

turns.en: The independence of thought is probably the least generic one of those. I think a lot of people want to be good and kind and work hard and whatever else.
turns.zh: '独立思考'大概是这几条里最不常见的一条。很多人都想善良、想努力工作、诸如此类。

turns.en: For both my parents, it was a moral issue. You cannot ever worry about what other people think. I'm far to that side of the spectrum, but I do think about it sometimes.
turns.zh: 对我父母双方来说，这是一个道德问题：你永远不可以为'别人怎么想你'而活。我在这条光谱上已经很偏向那个方向了，但有时候确实也会想别人怎么看。

turns.en: You do sometimes worry what other people think? Yeah. What do you want them to think? They worry that they don't? I worry about raising people's competitive hackles in the ecosystem.
turns.zh: 你有时候真的会担心别人怎么看你？会。那你希望他们怎么看你？他们难道反而不担心吗？

turns.en: Why? Because I'm a friendly person. I want to be friends with everybody. I don't mind competition, but the sometimes pure zero-sum competition stance of traditional Series A firms, Series A Series B firms that says, I'm going to own 18 to 25% of this company and take the board and you're going to own none of it.
turns.zh: 我担心在生态里挑起别人的好斗情绪。为什么？因为我是一个友好的人，我想和所有人做朋友。我不排斥竞争，但传统 A 轮、B 轮基金那种纯粹零和的竞争姿态——'我要占这家公司 18% 到 25%、还要拿董事会席位，而你一股都没有'——

turns.en: It's not conducive to a lot of collaboration. There are issues with that from an incentives perspective, but the public market's orientation, people are loved to tell you about their best ideas, pile in after them.
turns.zh: 不利于很多协作。从激励角度看那也有问题。但公开市场那种取向——人们乐于把最好的想法讲给你听，然后大家跟在他们后面一起买入——

turns.en: This is an extraordinary situation. I would love to talk about why gaming and entertainment is going to be totally different and people are super under-indexed on it.
turns.zh: 这种局面非常特别。我很愿意聊聊为什么游戏和娱乐行业会变得完全不同，而大家在这上面的敞口严重不足。

turns.en: There's part of that orientation that just appeals to me as very positive some person. I'm always interested in sources of inspiration. I'm curious in two ways, overall in your life, who has inspired you the most and also right now in this very moment, who is inspiring you the most and why?
turns.zh: 那种气质里有一部分，对我这种特别看重正和（positive-sum）的人非常有吸引力。我总是对灵感的来源感兴趣。我好奇两件事：总体来说，谁给你的启发最多？以及此时此刻，谁在激励你、为什么？

turns.en: I saw my parents build a company. I was like, this is so cool. It's us against the man. The man is very big company. The man is trying to kill us.
turns.zh: 我看着我的父母建起一家公司。我当时想：这也太酷了——'我们 vs. The Man'。The Man 是那些大公司，The Man 想弄死我们。

turns.en: We can still do it just because the technology is better. The product is better and the customer will want it. My love and ethos goes to entrepreneurs.
turns.zh: 但我们照样能赢，就因为我们的技术更好、产品更好、客户会想要它。我的爱和信条都属于创业者。

turns.en: You can make something out of nothing because you see a better future and you can do it really fast. These things appealed to me in terms of what I want to try.
turns.zh: 你可以无中生有，因为你看到了一个更好的未来，而且能很快做到。在'我想尝试什么'这个问题上，这些东西深深吸引着我。

turns.en: There's so much courage in that, in optimism. There is something poisonous that bothers me today where I think especially like the post-gen Z entrepreneurial crowd, I think it's like all marketing and brand is real.
turns.zh: 那里面有巨大的勇气和乐观。但今天有些有毒的东西让我不安：特别是 Z 世代之后的创业圈，我觉得一切都变成了营销和品牌。

turns.en: Building a network is totally real. No one denies that. But when folks are very cynical about how the world works, how entrepreneurship works, that it's just nepotism and Twitter is useful.
turns.zh: 搭建人脉当然是真实的，没人否认。但如果人们对世界如何运转、创业如何成功特别犬儒，觉得'不过是裙带关系加推特好使'——

turns.en: I think that's nonsense. If you focus on value and treating people well and you work with extraordinary people and the vision is worthwhile, that works more times than you think.
turns.zh: 我觉得那是胡说。只要你专注价值、善待他人，和非凡的人共事，愿景值得做——它成事的次数远超你想的。

turns.en: There's so much criticism about playing the game, be it marketing or fundraising, and I hate that. Cod is like this. I find him very inspiring.
turns.zh: 外界对'玩这套游戏'——无论是营销还是募资——批评太多，我很讨厌这种风气。Cod 让我很受启发。

turns.en: And Tuhun is like this. I find him very inspiring where he's just like, if we just do the right thing by the customer, we will win. Feels a lot more complicated than that.
turns.zh: Tuhun 也让我很受启发，他就是那种'只要我们善待客户、做对的事，我们就会赢'的人。虽然现实感觉比这复杂得多。

turns.en: I think he's right and that seems to be working. One of the huge debates right now is what to do about the fact that there are open source models not American made, which are competitive at the frontier of performance of AI models and seem to clearly have been at least to some degree based on the work of American models.
turns.zh: 我觉得他是对的，而且这条路看起来走得通。眼下最大的争论之一：那些非美国制造的开源模型，在前沿性能上已经具备竞争力，而且至少在一定程度上明显借鉴了美国模型的工作——这该怎么办？

turns.en: What to do about this? What it means for the future of AI? Companies love open source because they can build their own thing and base 10 and others that serve a lot of inference work with a lot of these models.
turns.zh: 该怎么办？这对 AI 的未来意味着什么？公司们喜欢开源，因为可以拿来做自己的东西；像 Base10 和其他做大量推理服务的公司，也广泛使用这些模型。

turns.en: How are you thinking about what's right? What should happen? What will happen? The implications for business? This is a big, hard, important, interesting question.
turns.zh: 你怎么思考什么是对的？应该发生什么？会发生什么？对商业的影响是什么？这是一个大、难、重要又有趣的问题。

turns.en: It's a big question. My point of view on what is healthy for businesses, America, the ecosystem, individuals, and then there's what's already actually happened.
turns.zh: 它确实很大。我的观点分两层：什么对商业、对美国、对生态、对个人是健康的；以及已经实际发生了什么。

turns.en: The reality is we have over the last three years increasingly competitive open source models from all fronts, largely China, but definitely also the U.S. and Europe.
turns.zh: 现实是，过去三年来自各方的开源模型越来越有竞争力，主要来自中国，但也确定有美国和欧洲的。

turns.en: Most recently, think-y poolside people waited for reflection, Nvidia models, Mistral. We will have very powerful and already do have very powerful open source models from Western countries.
turns.zh: 最近的有 Thinking、Poolside、Reflection、Nvidia 的模型、Mistral 等等。我们已经有、也会继续有非常强大的西方开源模型。

turns.en: The cat is out of the bag and these are in use everywhere. Even if you have no economic point of view on the labs and you just say, how is the diffusion of capability going to happen in the economy?
turns.zh: 精灵已经出了瓶子，这些模型无处不在地被使用。就算你对实验室没有经济层面的观点，只看'能力如何在经济体中扩散'——

turns.en: There are a huge number of instances where it is too expensive, too sensitive, or too slow to use the model from the frontier providers today.
turns.zh: ——也有海量场景，今天用前沿供应商的模型要么太贵、要么太敏感、要么太慢。

turns.en: I think that's going to increase as we learn how to do more things with AI because it's actually quite expensive. It's objectively true that if the capabilities are more democratized, you will see them used in more ways.
turns.zh: 我觉得随着我们学会用 AI 做更多事，这类场景还会更多，因为它确实很贵。客观事实是：能力越普惠，就会被越多方式使用。

turns.en: I want to see that happen. I do think that it would be irresponsible not to understand the safety profile of models as they progress because you just draw the line.
turns.zh: 我希望看到那发生。但我确实也认为，如果对模型随着进展的安全状况不做了解，那是不负责任的——因为你总要划一条线。

turns.en: We have companies that use frontier model capability for defensive cybersecurity and for biology work. If it works for those use cases, it obviously also should work in similar ways for the offensive use cases or the bioweapons biosecurity use cases.
turns.zh: 有些公司已经在用前沿模型的能力做防御性网络安全、做生物方面的工作。如果这些用例行得通，那它在进攻性用例、生物武器和生物安全用例上，显然也会以类似方式行得通。

turns.en: We just need to look at that reality and think about what are the other ways in which you control this, but attempting to stop technological progress and openness around it.
turns.zh: 我们需要正视这个现实，思考在推动技术进步与开放的同时，还有哪些方式能控制风险。

turns.en: If you did restrict use of open source models in the United States, you'd basically just restrict law-abiding American businesses and slow them down or move profits different pockets, prevent certain uses of them because the actual attackers or people who have adversarial uses of these things are not affected by your restrictions.
turns.zh: 如果你在美国限制开源模型的使用，实际上限制的只是守法的美国企业、拖慢它们，或者把利润挪到别的口袋——而真正的攻击者、那些恶意使用的人，根本不受你的限制影响。

turns.en: You're restricting your own people. My view would be there should be testing and understanding of these models at the frontier. People are very worried about backdoor-like behaviors in Chinese models.
turns.zh: 你限制的是自己人。我的看法是：应该对这些前沿模型做测试和了解。大家很担心中国模型里有后门式的行为。

turns.en: The thing to do would actually be have a very rigorous set of safety testing on that. Let's go find out as much as we can instead of talking about how there might be this issue in a speculative way where there's not been nearly enough actual research on it.
turns.zh: 该做的事其实是：对其实施一套非常严格的安全测试，尽可能搞清楚，而不是用推测的口吻说'可能有这个问题'——实际研究目前远远不够。

turns.en: The future where there is broad access to intelligence too cheap to meter, as Sam put it, that is coming. It will be supported by open source.
turns.zh: 一个智能'便宜到无需计量'的普及未来——用 Sam 的话说——正在到来，它会由开源来支撑。

turns.en: Businesses wanted to control their own destiny for economics, for capacity. If given those models and increasing democratization of the skills to post-train these models, build harnesses, use tasks, the economy is so big, every individual has these use cases that are not going to be imagined by a researcher in a frontier lab.
turns.zh: 企业出于经济性和容量考虑想掌控自己的命运。有了这些模型，加上后训练、搭 harness、做任务这些技能的普惠化——经济太大了，每个个体都有前沿实验室里的研究者想象不到的使用场景。

turns.en: You can't imagine the diversity of reality. Even if you trusted the models to go figure out what to do, they have to get there. The best way for that to happen is a ecosystem of businesses as we've always had in the economy, cheap infrastructure.
turns.zh: 你无法想象现实的多样性。哪怕你信任模型能自己想明白该做什么，它们也得先抵达那里。最好的路径，就是我们经济里一向拥有的那个生态：依托廉价基础设施的千行百业。

turns.en: Do you ever worry that an alternate version of US history is that there was energy too cheap to meter because we built 1,000 AP, 1,000s or something, much like China is doing now in nuclear?
turns.zh: 你有没有想过美国历史的另一个版本：能源也便宜到不用计量，因为我们像中国现在在核能上这样，建了一千座、几千座反应堆？

turns.en: Just a set of circumstances happen such that we just didn't get that. Do you ever worry about that as it relates to intelligence? It does seem inevitable that we're going to have abundant, accessible, low-cost, valuable intelligence.
turns.zh: 只不过一堆际遇让我们没建成。关于智能，你担心过同样的事吗？看起来，我们会拥有充沛、可及、低成本又有价值的智能，似乎是必然的。

turns.en: Can you imagine a world where we don't? Yes, absolutely. And I also think I can imagine very easily a world where we don't have that in a competitive way because it is essential to economic competitiveness and national security.
turns.zh: 你能想象一个没有这一切的世界吗？——能，完全可以。而且我也很容易想象一个即便拥有、却'没有竞争力'的世界，因为它对经济竞争力和国家安全至关重要。

turns.en: There is not a version of the world where we rebuild our industrial base without automation in the United States. If we don't import people and our people are expensive and we lack some of the skills but want to produce a lot more goods and have a more resilient supply chain.
turns.zh: 不存在这样一种版本：美国在没有自动化的情况下重建工业基础。我们要么不引进人口——我们的人力很贵、有些技能缺位——却又想生产更多商品、拥有更有韧性的供应链。

turns.en: It just doesn't matter. Who's going to produce this stuff? People in the United States do not want to work and should not want to work for $13 an hour doing a very inhuman job.
turns.zh: 那谁来生产这些东西？在美国，没人愿意、也不该愿意以每小时 13 美元干那种非常不人道的活儿。

turns.en: I don't think it is inevitable that we are competitive and I think we need to make that decision actively. The version of it that I think is very possible is that people are rationally afraid of the impact of AI on jobs or dislike the capture of rent by a small number of technology firms, rejecting the idea of being in the permanent underclass and then connecting that to a anti-capitalist orientation.
turns.zh: 我不觉得我们的竞争力是必然的，我认为必须主动做出那个决定。我觉得很可能的一个版本是：人们理性地惧怕 AI 对就业的冲击，或者厌恶少数科技公司攫取租金，抵触成为'永久底层'，然后把这一切和一种反资本主义的立场接上了轨。

turns.en: That contingent of thought can slow down build of energy and infrastructure and industrial capacity. One of the most important inputs is compute.
turns.zh: 这一思潮会拖慢能源、基础设施和工业产能的建设，而算力是最关键的投入之一。

turns.en: If we don't have it, we're naturally not competitive or we're at least not independent. I think we're going to start talking much more about compute independence.
turns.zh: 如果我们没有它，我们天然就没有竞争力，至少谈不上独立。我觉得我们会越来越多地谈论'算力独立'（compute independence）。

turns.en: That's a big problem. So on this point of compute independence, what does that mean? What are the missing pieces of compute independence? The most obvious one might be more leading edge fab capacity here in the US or something like this.
turns.zh: 这是个大问题。说到算力独立，它意味着什么？拼图缺的是哪几块？最显而易见的一块，也许是在美国建设更多最尖端的晶圆厂（fab）产能。

turns.en: There's all sorts of stuff upstream. There's particular kinds of glass, very important that's controlled by basically one company that TSMC has a monopoly on the supply of.
turns.zh: 上游还有各种各样的东西：某种玻璃特别关键，基本由一家公司掌控，TSMC 也在某些环节上垄断着供应。

turns.en: There's all these component parts, but if you think about compute independence, if so much boils down to compute, what's to be done about it?
turns.zh: 这些部件林林总总——但如果你想算力独立，如果说到底一切就归结为算力，那该怎么办？

turns.en: Are you trying to invest in companies that are solving that problem? What is the problem? Can you say a bit more about what it'll take? Well, if you just work backwards from a data center full of GPUs, cooling, powering, training and inference so we can support the use cases, all of those inputs, it actually looks a great deal like energy independence or something like that.
turns.zh: 你在投那些解决这个问题的公司吗？问题究竟是什么？能多讲讲要做到需要什么吗？——这么说吧，如果从装满 GPU 的数据中心往回倒推：散热、供电、训练、推理，为了支撑这些用例的一切投入，最后你会发现它非常像'能源独立'这件事。

turns.en: All those inputs, there is a global supply chain. I've got my TSMC mug with me. There are parts of that supply chain that are like a very thin sieve in a place that is not necessarily stable or accessible to the U.S. and allies.
turns.zh: 所有这些投入组成一条全球供应链。我手上就捧着印 TSMC logo 的马克杯。这条链上有几个环节像一道很细的筛网，而所在的地方未必稳定，也未必是美国和盟友能及的。

turns.en: A different version of the world that will take a bunch of investment and national security and energy policy is, for example, Jacob Helberg is working on something called Paxilica.
turns.zh: 要通往另一个版本的世界，需要大量投资、国家安全与能源政策。比如 Jacob Helberg 正在推动一个叫 Pax Silica 的计划。

turns.en: And it's like, okay, for every part of the supply chain, can we invest in more capacity and figure out what the independent paths are? I don't think that means it's all got to be created in the United States compared to advantageous real, but having more than one source is a position that everybody wants to be in.
turns.zh: 它的思路是：对供应链的每一个环节，我们能不能投资扩产能、找出可以独立的路径？我不觉得这意味着一切都要在美国制造——比起完全自给自足，'拥有不止一个供应来源'是人人都想处的位置。

turns.en: When we think about the components that we've invested in, we've invested in the labor gap for data centers and robotics, we've invested in nuclear energy, we've invested in alternative chip architectures.
turns.zh: 说到我们投过的组件：投了填数据中心劳动力缺口的公司，投了机器人，投了核能，还投了替代性芯片架构。

turns.en: We keep looking at people who are essentially data center builders, solar and battery installers of some kind. Part of this is the actual capacity builder.
turns.zh: 我们一直在看的那些人，本质上就是数据中心建设者、太阳能和储能安装商这类角色，其中一部分是真正的产能建造者。

turns.en: That's a very operational business, like somewhere between operations, some technology and real state. Financing. Yeah. And financing. Absolutely.
turns.zh: 那是非常运营型的生意，介于运营、某种技术和房地产之间。还有融资。对，还有融资，绝对。

turns.en: That's probably the dominant thing. We have not invested in it yet, despite looking very closely. I'm not opposed to it, but fundamentally, I'm a technology investor.
turns.zh: 那可能是主导性的东西。虽然我们看得很仔细，但还没投过。我不反对，但根本上我是个技术投资人。

turns.en: I want to understand what it is that is the durable product asset people are building. What are the base debates inside of conviction? You've got such an interesting team.
turns.zh: 我想理解人们到底在建什么能沉淀下来的产品资产。你们 Conviction 内部都在激辩什么？你们这支团队很有意思。

turns.en: Like your partner is a very technical person, amazing engineer. The young talent in your firm brings really interesting perspectives. So I'm imagining great, lively debates about things that matter, et cetera.
turns.zh: 比如你的合伙人本身是极强的技术人、出色的工程师，你团队里的年轻人才带来很多很有意思的视角。所以我在想象：一定有很多围绕重要问题的精彩激辩。

turns.en: What are the big debates today? A lot and I have a podcast called NoPriors. This premise of some of the things you believed, especially about markets as a pastor, like no longer true, is an interesting one.
turns.zh: 今天的大辩论题是什么？——特别多。我有个播客叫 No Priors，它的核心前提之一就是：你过去相信的一些事，特别是对市场的很多信念，可能已经不再成立。

turns.en: And regularly, we look at companies in domains that are not traditional software domains. Not even traditional software domains, but can you make money in this market at all?
turns.zh: 我们经常在那些并不传统的软件领域里看公司——甚至都谈不上传统软件——核心问题是：这个市场到底能不能赚钱？

turns.en: Venture investing in semis companies, lip-boot-tan aside, was like a god-awful business for the longest time. The returns. Everyone told me this.
turns.zh: 长久以来，半导体公司的风险投资——Lip-Bu Tan 除外——是一门惨不忍睹的生意，看那个回报率就知道了。这话谁都在跟我说。

turns.en: Yes. It was really bad. That's like an example of Bella, a partner on our team, started looking at a bunch of these companies and it's obvious that the demand is there.
turns.zh: 对，是真的糟糕。这就举一个例子：我们团队的合伙人 Bella 开始看一批这类公司，很明显需求是在的。

turns.en: Now I think we have arrived at the conclusion that others are as well, which is, well, the market is different today. We are seeing consolidated at scale demand for accelerators or even supply chain independence because the big buyers of it wanted to.
turns.zh: 现在我想我们和大家一样得出了结论：今天的市场不一样了。我们看到对加速器的整合式、规模化需求，甚至供应链独立的需求——因为大客户们想要这样。

turns.en: We can't all be stuck on one line, a GSMC. All of that is very, very valuable and that changes the risk equation for these companies. We start with pretty aligned beliefs about the direction of travel or the problems that are worth working on.
turns.zh: '我们总不能所有人都卡在同一条产线上、都受制于 TSMC。'这些都极其有价值，也改变了这类公司的风险等式。我们起手就有一组高度一致的信念：方向往哪走、哪些难题值得做。

turns.en: And then a lot of the debates are like, is the market friendly to a venture-backed company or not? Space is not a friendly market to a venture-backed company, but it's a possible.
turns.zh: 然后很多辩论就变成了：这个市场对风险投资支持的公司到底友好不友好？太空不是一个对风投友好的市场——

turns.en: Is the distribution of outcomes worth betting on? That could be true in solar and batteries and nuclear in turbine manufacturing, in robotics and biology.
turns.zh: ——但它是可能的。关键是：结果的分布值不值得下注？这在太阳能、电池、核能、涡轮机制造、机器人和生物领域都可能成立。

turns.en: These are not your favorite software markets from 10 years ago. Each of them is a new debate. Biology is an interesting one where by virtue of seeing the data empirically, I have now strongly moved to one side of the debate.
turns.zh: 这些都不是十年前那种'你最爱的软件市场'。每一个都是新的辩论题。生物学很有意思：因为亲眼看到了数据，我现在已经强烈地站到了辩论的一边。

turns.en: What side is that? You can create and capture enormous value with models in biology. And there could be different AI software in biology. We're the first check in a company called Chai Discovery.
turns.zh: 哪一边？——用模型在生物学里可以创造并捕获巨大价值，也可以有'AI for biology'的软件公司。我们是 Chai Discovery 这家公司的第一张支票。

turns.en: And Chai is working with a number of top 10 pharma companies in really significant ways to accelerate some part of the R&D process. The conventional wisdom, when we invest in this company, and I've been looking at computational biology companies of different sorts for five plus years at that point, the conventional wisdom was the only way you make money in biotech or serving pharma is by make a drug
turns.zh: Chai 正在与好几家 top 10 制药公司深度合作，加速研发流程中的某些环节。我们投它的时候——那时我看各种计算生物学公司已经五年多了——传统智慧是：想在 biotech 或者'为 pharma 服务'里赚钱，唯一的办法是做药——

turns.en: and then get bio-buck's deals and then decide how far along that risk path you want to take and what that means for the capital structure of the company is, okay, the great traditional biotech firms find these principal investigators and they own 40% of the company and they're kind of assembling these things, turning them into candidates.
turns.zh: ——然后拿 biobucks（里程碑对价）式的交易，再决定你愿意沿那条风险路径走多远、它对公司的资本结构意味着什么。传统的 biotech 大机构去找那些首席研究员，占公司 40%，把项目攒起来，推进成候选药物。

turns.en: But most of it doesn't work. So it's just like a very different distribution of outcomes and structure and way to invest in businesses. Dumb software investors, you can't make money selling software to pharma or build platform businesses at pharma.
turns.zh: 但大多数都不成。所以那是完全不同的结果分布、结构和投资生意的方式。传统智慧还说：卖给 pharma 软件赚不到钱，在 pharma 里建不成平台公司。

turns.en: The debate is, does it change with models? I'm a strong yes. Now, we still have a question to solve on regulatory. There's the speed of the physical world and safety is not something you can overcome easily, but I think we should see a massive acceleration in cures.
turns.zh: 争论点就是：有了模型，这会不会变？我是强烈的'会'。当然，监管上还有问题要解决；物理世界的速度和'安全'也不是轻易能绕过的。但我认为我们会看到药物研发大规模提速。

turns.en: What flipped that for you? Evidence, did you see from we don't know yet? We invested when we didn't know yet. That's part of the fun of venture.
turns.zh: 是什么让你转变的？你看到了证据，还是本来就不知道？——我们投的时候还没有答案。'在还不知道的时候下注'，这正是风投的乐趣。

turns.en: We were like, it is possible that it was worth trying. It could happen, yeah. There's no genius here. That's a $10 million contract. The other piece is actually you just talk to the scientist at the customer or somebody who leads a user of the tool or you see there are also end user adopted tools, product-led gross tools that are working in the space.
turns.zh: 我们当时就是觉得：这事值得一试，有可能成真。这里没有什么天才操作。那就是一个 1,000 万美元的合同。另一部分其实很简单：去和客户那边的科学家聊、和这个工具使用方的负责人聊。你也看得到，这个领域已经有靠终端用户自发采纳、产品驱动增长（product-led growth）的工具跑通了的。

turns.en: Well, the customer knows if it's valuable or not. The light bulb moment for the industry is when we will have a new indication or a new drug that clearly the trajectory of the thing was changed, created by AI.
turns.zh: 嗯，客户知道它到底有没有价值。整个行业的'点灯时刻'，会是出现一个新的适应症或一款新药——它的轨迹清清楚楚是被 AI 改变的。

turns.en: We should see a huge wave of investment and rightfully so, but it's going to happen. I'm very impressed by the speed with which pharma and healthcare overall has some, yes, this is going to make a difference and we actually think it's going to change the business.
turns.zh: 那时我们理应看到一波巨大的投资，但它一定会来。pharma 和整个医疗健康行业接受这件事的速度让我印象深刻——是的，这会带来真实的改变，我们真的认为它会改变这门生意。

turns.zh: 访问 workos.com，跳过那些不体面的基础设施苦活，专注你的产品。——你们为什么叫它 Conviction？——那是一种志向。最早期投资最传统的形式是：尽早跟上一家公司，仓位够大，永不卖出，然后陪着公司干——要么干成，要么阵亡。

turns.en: Wonderful alignment and simplicity to that. Mike and I have both had the benefit of being part of the journey for some companies where it took a minute to begin to work, or it's not obvious at the beginning.
turns.zh: 那会带来多么美妙的对齐和简单。Mike 和我都有幸陪伴过一些公司的旅程——它们花了段时间才开始起势，或者开局并不起眼。

turns.en: Sigma, Notion, Rippling. You wouldn't bet on a company hoping that it's going to take four or five years to find the thing. I think everybody is a product of their own experiences, including investing experiences.
turns.zh: Sigma、Notion、Rippling。你不会赌一家公司，然后干等四五年才找到那个东西。我觉得每个人都是自己经历的产物，投资经历也不例外。

turns.en: The first couple years at base 10 were very non-obvious as well. The ability to take a point of view that is not obvious in the market, because the market or because the people's backgrounds, whatever reason, and then just suspend doubt and act with full belief until it's true or not.
turns.zh: 在 Base10 的头几年也非常'不显然'。那种能力——在市场、或者因为人们各自的背景等各种原因还看不清的时候，持有一个非共识的观点，然后悬置怀疑、全力以赴地相信，直到它为真或为假。

turns.en: That's a great way to be a partner to somebody building a business. I'm trying to build a partnership, and I deeply believe this is a team sport.
turns.zh: 对于一个正在创业的人来说，那是特别好的合伙方式。我想建成的是一个 partnership，我深深相信这是一场团队运动。

turns.en: I was talking to a friend who runs another investing firm where he is like, we don't have individual ownership of our investments. I'm like, that is nonsense to me.
turns.zh: 我有一位朋友也在经营投资公司，他说'我们的投资不设个人负责人'。我当时就想：这在我听来完全是胡扯。

turns.en: How could you run a business that way? Because somebody has to own the decision. I don't know if this is right or wrong, but I don't know any other way to invest by saying, Patrick, you must make the decision.
turns.zh: 生意怎么能这么经营？总得有人对这个决策负责。不知道这算对还是错，但除了说'Patrick，这个决策必须由你来做'，我不知道还能怎么投资。

turns.en: Do you believe, convince us, how can we help you make that decision? What have you learned about risk-taking? Behind conviction, it sounds like there is often a leap of faith of some sort.
turns.zh: '那你怎么想？说服我们，我们怎么帮你做这个决策？'——关于承担风险，你学到了什么？听起来，conviction 的背后往往总要有某种信念之跃（leap of faith）。

turns.en: Obviously, if you knew everything and it was obvious, that would be priced in and there'd be no return opportunity. Is there always a leap of faith?
turns.zh: 显然，如果你什么都知道、而且一切都是显然的，那早就被定价了，也就没有回报机会了。信念之跃是永远存在的吗？是'承担风险'的另一种说法吗？

turns.en: Is that risk-taking by another name? Unlike my good friends at Founders Fund, I don't have an instinct to be contrarian, but I do think it is so fundamental to decide what you think and not worry too much about what other people think.
turns.zh: ——不像 Founders Fund 我那几位好朋友，我并没有唱反调的本能。但我确实认为，最根本的是想清楚你自己怎么想，不要太在意别人怎么想。

turns.en: Other people is the dominant narratives of the period or even what different players in the ecosystem that are really important declare one way or another.
turns.zh: '别人'就是那个时代的主导叙事，甚至是生态里那些举足轻重的玩家或此或彼的表态。

turns.en: I think you just need to find the truth. The way I would relate that to risk-taking is if you find the truth and it is wrongly priced and you hold on to that, you're in a good position.
turns.zh: 我觉得你只要找到真相。我把这和投资中的风险承担联系起来：如果你找到了真相，而它被错误定价，你又拿得住，你就处在一个好位置。

turns.en: You want asymmetric information and then the confidence to hold the opinion when other people haven't come around to it yet. I think a lot about how to make sure we have the information that is better than other peoples and then protect ourselves from noise.
turns.zh: 你要的是信息上的不对称，以及在别人还没转向之前把观点拿住的自信。我花很多心思思考怎么确保我们的信息比别人更好，然后把自己从噪声里保护起来。

turns.en: Describe that in one more level of detail. That's a great way of asking what conviction looks like today. You're building that shell. What are the keys to doing those two things well, both having the truth and protecting yourself from the noise?
turns.zh: 再展开一层讲讲。这其实就是在问今天的 conviction 长什么样——你在打造的那个'护壳'。把这两件事都做好——既掌握真相、又隔绝噪声——关键是什么？

turns.en: I want to spend my time when I'm learning about the world from somebody who is making it happen, our portfolio founders or the many founders who are doing amazing things outside of portfolio, who are doing something that surprises me or advances the frontier or really smart believe something I don't.
turns.zh: 我想把时间花在：当我要认识世界时，向正在创造它的人学习——我们的组合创始人，或者大量在组合之外做着非凡事情的创业者——他们做的事让我意外、推进了前沿，或者聪明人相信了我还不信的东西。

turns.en: These are three different categories. I'll give you an example. Mikey Shulman at SUNO is building an amazing business doing music generation.
turns.zh: 这是三个不同的类别。我给你举个例子：SUNO 的 Mikey Shulman 正在做音乐生成，建了一个了不起的生意。

turns.en: Shame on me. I knew Mikey, a mutual friend of ours who was an investor, asked me to invest and I stupidly said no. I was just like, I don't think that many people want to make music.
turns.zh: 惭愧。我认识 Mikey，我们的一个共同朋友——他是投资人——他让我来投，我愚蠢地说了不。我当时就想：我不觉得有那么多人想'做'音乐。

turns.en: I make music. But can you turn into a social network? How much consumption is there going to be? A lot of questions. My intuition is just wrong.
turns.zh: 做音乐的人是有一些，但这能变成一个社交网络吗？消费端会有多大？问题太多了。我的直觉当时就是错的。

turns.en: It's been actually somewhat wrong because I have underestimated the amount of expression or entertainment and creation for a lot of AI tools.
turns.zh: 而且错得还不轻——因为我低估了 AI 工具里'表达、娱乐与创作'的量级。

turns.en: I've learned something here by talking to Mikey about his business and what people are trying to do. So, if it is founders who have companies that are creating a behavior you don't understand, actually working on a research in an interesting direction, businesses that are like, here's my plan for AI, all that is super educational, I think the secular logic sometimes of what do people believe about the big lab strategy today?
turns.zh: 通过与 Mikey 聊他的生意、聊人们想做什么，我在这里上了一课。所以：创业者做出了你看不懂的新行为、有人在朝有意思的方向做研究、有公司拿着'这就是我针对 AI 的计划'来找你——这些都极具教育意义。我觉得那种'大势逻辑'——比如今天人们怎么相信大实验室的战略——

turns.en: How can any of the applications live? It's actually not that instructive for your decision making. The way I think of it is any organization has a couple of key priorities.
turns.zh: ——应用层公司凭什么能活？——其实对你的决策没什么指导意义。我的思考方式是：任何组织都有几个关键的优先事项。

turns.en: Let's assume the priority for open AI and anthropic team mind is AGI or ASI in a safe way where they capture a lot of profit. The priorities that ladder into that probably look like chat GPT, ads, coding, maybe there's an expansion after that, co-work, the ability to get different types of users to do richer tasks and more interfaces.
turns.zh: 假设 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 团队的优先级是安全地实现 AGI 或 ASI，并捕获大量利润。往上追溯的优先级，看起来大概像 ChatGPT、广告、编程，之后可能会有扩张：Cowork——让更多种类的用户完成更丰富的任务、接入更多界面。

turns.en: I think you have to judge the actual competitiveness of any of those efforts, the reasonable scope of them, and then look at them relative to each of our companies or opportunities that we're looking at.
turns.zh: 我觉得你要判断这些努力实际的竞争力和合理的边界，然后拿它们逐一对照我们在看的每家公司、每个机会。

turns.en: Coming up with some grand strategic framework for what layer is going to win here, I think is not useful to me, and I feel like people spend so much of their investing energy thinking about versus, I want to spend my energy figuring out, if we're 1% of the way in, what is the next 99% of diffusion?
turns.zh: 至于搞一个宏大战略框架去判断'哪一层会赢'，我觉得对我没什么用。我感觉大家把太多投资精力花在'对抗'上——而我想把精力花在：如果我们才走完 1%，剩下的 99% 的扩散是什么样子？

turns.en: That's where we try to direct our energy. For fun, as we wind down here, understanding this is like a purely speculative question and it's meant more fun than raw prediction, what are some things you think are true a year from now?
turns.zh: 那就是我们想发力的地方。好了，收尾之前来点轻松的。先说好，这是个纯投机的问题，重在好玩而不是预测——一年后，你觉得有哪些事会变成真的？

turns.en: Based on all these incredible people that you're close with, the research community, the entrepreneurs like the Sunday founders, you add it all up, things are moving fast.
turns.zh: 基于你身边那些了不起的人、研究社区、像 Dyna 创始人这样的创业者——把这些全加起来，事情推进得太快了。

turns.en: A year is a long time and it's like reverse dog years now. What do you think is notably different about the world of technology a year from now?
turns.zh: 一年可是很长时间，而且现在就像'反向狗年'。你觉得一年后技术世界会有什么显著不同？

turns.en: I'm hopeful that a year from now, we see Germans paradox in practice as we have agents and products that do more of the mundane more effectively in all the domains of our lives.
turns.zh: 我希望一年后能看到杰文斯悖论（Jevons paradox）在现实中上演：当智能体（agents）和产品把生活各领域里琐碎的事干得更好更多时，

turns.en: It should look like the transformation that has happened in software engineering. You have companies, I have companies where they're like, we're just going way faster.
turns.zh: 它应该看起来像软件工程已经经历的那场转型。有些公司——我投的公司里就有——会说'我们就是在飞速变快'。

turns.en: I expect that some analogy like that will happen everywhere else. We see it in our companies where in one of our portfolio companies, the marketing department is like a person in the house.
turns.zh: 我预计类似的类比会在所有其他地方发生。我们自己 portfolio 里就看到过：一家组合公司的市场部基本上就一个人。

turns.en: This is a company that serves lots of customers. They need to do very traditional things, sales and even content. What happened was the guy in charge of marketing is interested in creating leverage for himself.
turns.zh: 那是一家服务大量客户的公司，要做非常传统的事——销售、内容。发生的事情是：管营销的那个人热衷于给自己创造杠杆。

turns.en: He's like, I made an autonomous marketing department for us, the company. In every function, as you learn faster, do less of the mundane, you will repurpose that time somehow.
turns.zh: 他说：'我为我们公司造了一个自主运转的营销部门。'在任何职能里，当你学得更快、少做琐事，你总会把省下的时间重新用在别处。

turns.en: Do you work less now that you are more productive with AI? Yeah, I work more. I think this is like a core wisdom of Jensen's, which is we're all going to be more employed.
turns.zh: 既然 AI 让你更高效，你工作变少了吗？——不，我工作更多了。我觉得这是 Jensen 的核心智慧之一：我们所有人都会更'受雇'、更忙。

turns.en: We need to make sure that people are given access and education to the tooling that will allow that to happen. What you built is incredible.
turns.zh: 我们要确保人们拿到接触这些工具的机会、接受相应的教育，让这件事成为可能。你建成的一切真了不起。

turns.en: We've loved through the Colossus side getting to know your whole world. It's so distinctive. You are a great example that there's always room for great, meaning there was plenty of early stage investment firms when you started Conviction, and yet here we are four years later, whatever, and if you ask the people you've worked with, you've made a real huge difference in their lives.
turns.zh: 通过 Colossus 认识你的整个世界，我们特别喜欢。它太独一份了。你就是一个绝佳的证明：'优秀'永远有位置——你创办 Conviction 的时候，早期投资基金一大把，可四年后的今天，看看我们坐在这儿；去问问和你共事过的人，你真的巨大地改变了他们的生活。

turns.en: There's just always room for great. I think that's a great, awesome lesson, especially because I love how you described the early pitch was not like, here's how we're differentiated at every level of the funnel.
turns.zh: '优秀永远有位置'。这是特别了不起的一课，尤其因为我很喜欢你说的那种最早的 pitch——不是'我们在漏斗的每一层如何差异化'，

turns.en: We're just going to run at this thing. By the end, I got so frustrated that I was just like, it's an execution game. Totally. I ask everyone the same traditional closing question.
turns.zh: 而是'我们就是要朝这件事狂奔'。说到最后，我都被烦到了：这本来就是个执行的游戏。完全同意。我要问每个人那个传统的收尾问题。

turns.en: What is the kindest thing that anyone's ever done for you? I love this question. I'm going to give a collective answer. I think there are so many people who are extraordinarily accomplished in Silicon Valley who care very little for pedigree as soon as they have conversation with you, and they're like, maybe you can help me or you have an interesting idea, or maybe I just think you're promising.
turns.zh: 别人为你做过的最善良的事是什么？我太爱这个问题了。我打算给一个'集体'的答案。硅谷有很多成就非凡的人，几乎不太在意门第——只要跟你聊上一个对话，他们就会想：也许你能帮到我，也许你的想法有意思，或者我就是觉得你这个人有潜力。

turns.en: The dominant factor in their own willingness to invest in a relationship or a person is just their assessment of the idea in the person. I think that's amazing.
turns.zh: 在他们愿意为一段关系、一个人下注这件事上，主导因素就是对'这个想法、这个人'本身的评估。我觉得这很了不起。

turns.en: That is not how most ecosystems work. Ashim Channa and Anil Bastery and Joseph Ansonnelli and Reed Hoffman who hired me at Greylock, I started when I was 23.
turns.zh: 多数生态并不是这样运转的。Ashim Channa、Anil Bastery、Joseph Ansonnelli，还有在 Greylock 把我招进来的 Reed Hoffman——我 23 岁就入行了。

turns.en: People love to make fun of young VCs where they're like, what a barnacle on the ecosystem. Is it a terrible experience for entrepreneurs? I don't know anything.
turns.zh: 人们爱拿年轻 VC 开涮，说他们是'生态上的藤壶'，'让创业者体验很糟吧？他什么都不懂。'

turns.en: They're trying to advise people who gave this kid money, and I'm like, one, my job is just to make other people successful at the time. You can take any task in any job and just try to be great at the task with mimicry and first principles thinking.
turns.zh: 他们好像在给'给这小孩投了钱的人'出主意。而我当时想：第一，我的职责就是让别人成功。你可以拿任何工作里的任何任务，靠模仿和第一性原理思考，努力把这个任务做到极致。

turns.en: We hire earlier career people at my firm, but I do think, oh my goodness, thank you for taking a shot on some random person and then investing the time to teach me how to be an investor.
turns.zh: 我们基金也招更早期职业生涯的人。但我心里真的会感慨：天哪，谢谢你们在一个无名小卒身上下注，还花时间教我怎么做投资人。

turns.en: I think there were a few people who gave me advice starting the firm who, I think they would think of this as entirely trivial. I'm just giving you my opinion, but Ravi Gupta, who is now co-CEO of a new thing called Ithaca, Dylan Field and Elena Natalinsky, John Lilly, who's been a long time partner and friend.
turns.zh: 我觉得有几位在我建基金初期给过我建议的人，自己可能觉得那轻如鸿毛——'我只是给你个观点而已'——但比如 Ravi Gupta，他现在是新公司 Ithaca 的联席 CEO，还有 Dylan Field、Elena Natalinsky，以及 longtime 伙伴和朋友 John Lilly。

turns.en: There are a few folks who were just like, you can definitely do it. I was going to do it either way, but having the encouragement of people who believed that there was room to be great and including some of our first LPs, I will be forever grateful to, I guess, the people who took a risk with me.
turns.zh: 有几个人就是会说一句：你绝对做得到。反正我无论如何都要做的，但那些相信'这里存在做得很伟大的空间'的人的鼓励——也包括我们最早的一些 LP——我会永远感恩，感恩那些愿意陪我一起冒险的人。

turns.en: It's beautiful the world runs on faith, belief without evidence yet, and still conviction in someone's ability to do something. Pretty cool.
turns.zh: 很美妙——这个世界是靠'信'运转的：还没有证据，就先相信一个人能把某件事做成。挺酷的。

turns.en: It's faith in people. We talked a lot about how people's ideas and our opinions of them are intertwined, but I think that's a beautiful thing because you don't need any particular advantage to have an idea.
turns.zh: 是对人的信念。我们聊了很多——人的想法和我们对他人的评价是如何交织的。但我觉得这是件美好的事，因为拥有一个想法不需要任何特定的优势。

turns.en: The fact that folks will evaluate that and put faith in us, I could not be more grateful. I've learned a lot watching you operate and talking to you.
turns.zh: 而人们愿意去评估这个想法、把信任放在我们身上，我感激不尽。观察你怎么做事、和你聊天，我学到太多了。
